title: Intervention Efforts Failing to Turn Tide for Yen - 3-Minutes MLIV
titleChinese: 干预努力未能扭转日元走势 - 3分钟MLIV
summary: 日本和美国的干预努力未能扭转日元走势，尽管有多轮确认的干预和美国财政部长的警告，日元仍然表现不佳。分析人士认为，日本央行没有发挥作用，美联储加息预期和地缘政治因素也是影响因素，市场需要看到伊朗战争结束和油价下降，非农就业人数数据将是本周的重要数据点，可能会影响美联储的决策和市场走势。

transcript.english: Adam, are we still thinking about the yen this morning?
transcript.chinese: Adam，我们今天早上还在关注日元吗？

transcript.english: mean, to some extent, this was yesterday's real area of focus, wasn't it?
transcript.chinese: 我是说，在某种程度上，这昨天的真正关注点，不是吗？

transcript.english: But today we see the yen underperforming a little bit, and that's perhaps not what those who want a stronger yen wanted to see.
transcript.chinese: 但今天我们看到日元表现略微欠佳，这可能不是那些希望日元走强的人所期望的。

transcript.english: So what's our latest conclusion as to whether this intervention by the Japanese and the Americans will work?
transcript.chinese: 那么，我们最新的结论是什么，关于日本和美国的干预是否会有效？

transcript.english: Yeah, think when you consider the fact that we've had, you know, a couple of confirmed rounds of intervention now, which is also coordinated with the U .S.
transcript.chinese: 是的，考虑到我们已经有了，你知道的，几轮确认的干预，而且这些干预也与美国协调一致。

transcript.english: and have warnings from the U Treasury Secretary Besson, it's been particularly disappointing.
transcript.chinese: 并且美国财政部长贝森发出警告，结果却特别令人失望。

transcript.english: mean, even at the trough, we didn't really break through the May lows.
transcript.chinese: 即使是在低点，我们也没有真正突破五月份的低点。

transcript.english: I think the Japanese officials would have been hoping they would have got below 1 .55.
transcript.chinese: 我认为日本官员原本希望能跌破1.55。

transcript.english: So think when you also consider the positioning backdrop, I yen shorts, they were higher since July 2024.
transcript.chinese: 因此，当你考虑到仓位背景时，日元空头头寸自2024年7月以来一直处于较高水平。

transcript.english: Dollar positioning was at record highs on some measures.
transcript.chinese: 根据某些衡量指标，美元仓位处于历史新高。

transcript.english: It's a pretty pitiful response from what we've seen.
transcript.chinese: 从我们看到的来看，反应相当惨淡。

transcript.english: And I think, you know, ultimately, there's a couple of things at play here.
transcript.chinese: 而我认为，归根结底，有几件事在这里起作用。

transcript.english: One is that the BOJ just isn't playing its role.
transcript.chinese: 一方面是日本央行没有发挥其应有的作用。

transcript.english: We kind of get this continued communication effort from them that they may do something at some point in the future.
transcript.chinese: 我们一直收到他们的持续沟通，他们可能在未来某个时候采取行动。

transcript.english: In a world, there's price of Fed hikes that just isn't good enough.
transcript.chinese: 在一个世界里，美联储加息的预期并不是足够的。

transcript.english: And we saw some angst about the BOJ overnight.
transcript.chinese: 我们看到日本央行（BOJ）隔夜引发了一些担忧。

transcript.english: So that's soft 10 -year JGB auction as well.
transcript.chinese: 因此，10年期日本国债（JGB）拍卖也较为疲软。

transcript.english: So that's also front of mind.
transcript.chinese: 所以这也在人们的脑海中。

transcript.english: But also as well, quite simply from a geopolitical standpoint, with something out of control for Japanese officials, is that they need this war to end.
transcript.chinese: 但是从地缘政治角度来看，日本官员无法控制的事情是，他们需要这场战争结束。

transcript.english: They need oil prices to come lower.
transcript.chinese: 他们需要油价下降。

transcript.english: Yeah, so it's actually it's kind of a waste of money on this intervention unless you get a step in from the BOJ.
transcript.chinese: 是的，实际上，如果没有日本央行的跟进，这次干预有点浪费钱。

transcript.english: Just on that geopolitical point, you know, the headlines flying around, the comments flying around, Donald Trump being pretty angry towards Iran, them saying that the talks aren't even happening.
transcript.chinese: 就那一点地缘政治而言，你知道，到处都是头条新闻和评论，唐纳德·特朗普对伊朗相当愤怒，他们说谈判甚至都没有发生。

transcript.english: What does the market need to have greater progress?
transcript.chinese: 市场需要什么才能取得更大的进展？

transcript.english: Yeah, I mean, I think there's a pretty high bar at the moment for success.
transcript.chinese: 是的，我认为目前成功的门槛相当高。

transcript.english: You know, we saw Trump be relatively bullish on the prospects over the weekend.
transcript.chinese: 你知道，我们看到特朗普在周末对前景相对乐观。

transcript.english: And the same time Iran was talking about the Strait of Hormuz, it wasn't even about the full reopening of it.
transcript.chinese: 同时，伊朗在讨论霍尔木兹海峡时，并没有提到完全重新开放它。

transcript.english: And traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is still particularly low.
transcript.chinese: 霍尔木兹海峡的交通流量仍然特别低。

transcript.english: Then in other parts of the Middle East, traffic flows are relatively low.
transcript.chinese: 然后，在中东的其他地区，交通流量相对较低。

transcript.english: I think, you know, obviously, we need to see Trump's bullish on the weekend reciprocated from Iran.
transcript.chinese: 我认为，你知道，显然，我们需要看到伊朗在周末对特朗普的看涨情绪做出回应。

transcript.english: But we're just simply not seeing that at the moment.
transcript.chinese: 但是，我们目前并没有看到这种情况。

transcript.english: They're just saying that, you know, the US needs to change its behaviour.
transcript.chinese: 他们只是说，你知道的，美国需要改变其行为。

transcript.english: And I think even if we do get an interim peace agreement, then I think the markets can be particularly wary of it, given that we've already had one broken down.
transcript.chinese: 我认为，即使我们达成临时和平协议，我认为市场也会特别警惕，因为我们已经经历了一次破裂。

transcript.english: And then since the onset of the conflict, as far as I can tell, there's been no progress on nuclear.
transcript.chinese: 然后，自冲突开始以来，据我所知，核问题上没有取得任何进展。

transcript.english: So I think, you know, energy prices will stay sticky.
transcript.chinese: 所以，我认为，你知道的，能源价格将保持坚挺。

transcript.english: And in that environment, upside for bonds is limited, you know, particularly in the US, where there's a real rate story, and then also for Europe.
transcript.chinese: 在这种环境下，债券的上涨空间是有限的，你知道的，特别是在美国，有一个实际利率的故事，欧洲也是如此。

transcript.english: Yeah.
transcript.chinese: 是。

transcript.english: Let me ask you about the data point of the week, which is nonfarm payrolls due on Friday, of course, Adam.
transcript.chinese: 让我问你一下本周的数据点，即非农就业报告，当然是在周五，亚当。

transcript.english: Are we concerned?
transcript.chinese: 我们担心吗？

transcript.english: last week we saw that steepener trade, partly due to the Fed narrative rather than the data.
transcript.chinese: 上周我们看到收益率曲线陡峭化交易，部分原因是由于美联储的说法而不是数据。

transcript.english: But we don't really know how the Fed is going to react to data.
transcript.chinese: 但是我们真的不知道美联储将如何对数据做出反应。

transcript.english: That's by design, Kevin Warsh has told us.
transcript.chinese: 这就是设计的初衷，凯文·沃尔什曾经告诉我们。

transcript.english: So how are you thinking the market could respond then to this nonfarm payrolls?
transcript.chinese: 那么，你认为市场会如何应对这份非农就业报告呢？

transcript.english: Yeah, mean, it's a big data point.
transcript.chinese: 是的，我的意思是，这是一个重要的数据点。

transcript.english: You know, we need to play the ball, not the referee, Kevin Warsh says.
transcript.chinese: 凯文·沃尔什说，我们需要关注数据本身，而不是评判决策者。

transcript.english: And any data point now is a much higher vol event than it otherwise would have been.
transcript.chinese: 现在，任何数据点都比原本预期的更容易引发大幅波动。

transcript.english: There's plenty of scope to reprice a September hike, only priced around 65%.
transcript.chinese: 有足够的空间重新计入九月加息预期，目前仅有65%的概率被计入。

transcript.english: I think it's more interesting if we get a hot report.
transcript.chinese: 我认为如果我们看到强于预期的数据会更有趣。

transcript.english: Do markets really ramp up these wagers at the front end?
transcript.chinese: 市场真的会在收益率曲线短端推高这些工资吗？

transcript.english: I think the Fed's getting behind the curve.
transcript.chinese: 我认为美联储正在落后于形势。

transcript.english: But also the back end of the curve, there's a real rate story, which is really driving things as well.
transcript.chinese: 但收益率曲线长端也存在一个实际利率的故事，这也在推动着事态的发展。

transcript.english: We saw strong ISM yesterday.
transcript.chinese: 我们昨天看到强劲的ISM数据。

transcript.english: And if you see a strong NFP, do we start getting 30-year yields towards 5.3%?
transcript.chinese: 如果你看到强劲的非农就业报告，我们是否开始看到30年期收益率接近5.3%？

transcript.english: And that has also become a cross asset story as well.
transcript.chinese: 这也成为了一条影响多类资产的交易主线。
